diff: """Volleyball event detection: the whole system, as code. This file is what evolves.
Seed version: Gemini 4 Argon watches every 30 s clip (5 fps, high resolution, thinking high) with
the prompt evolved by evo2; overlapping clips are merged in code. No reviewer, no checks."""
the prompt evolved by evo2; overlapping clips are merged in code. Then one serve per rally, and a
serve-timing check: Argon watches 5 s at 10 fps around each serve and re-times it."""
PROMPT = """This is a volleyball match. This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match and runs for {length} seconds.
List every serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill and block you see. Follow these logging rules:
- Do not log routine sets during a rally; only log a set if it directly precedes a point-winning kill.
- Only log a block if it is a stuff block that directly ends the rally; do not log block jumps or soft block deflections where play continues.

- Never log both an attack and a kill for the same hit: if the spike wins the point, log it only as a kill; otherwise log it as an attack. Only log actual spikes/attack hits; never log soft free-ball passes or standing bumps sent over the net as attacks.
- Only log a dig when a defender successfully keeps an opponent's attack in play; never log a routine free-ball pass or a failed defensive touch or shank after a point-winning kill.
t      - the time in absolute match seconds (clip start {start} + offset)
type   - serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill or block
number - the player's shirt number, or null
error  - true if it was an error
point  - true if it won the point"""
MERGE_WINDOW = 0.4     # same type within this many seconds across overlapping clips = one event
answer = match.watch(name, prompt, fps=5, media="high", thinking="high")
return [e for evs in match.map(one, match.clips) for e in evs]
"""Overlapping clips see the same touch twice: keep the copy furthest from its clip's edge."""
for e in sorted(events, key=lambda x: x["t"]):
prior = next((o for o in reversed(out) if e["t"] - o["t"] <= MERGE_WINDOW and o["type"] == e["type"]), None)

SERVE_CHECK = """This {length:g} s video is cut from a volleyball match filmed side-on; it starts at 0.0 s. The {team} team plays on the {side} of the net, and a {team} player serves somewhere in this video. The server stands behind the {side} end line and is often outside the frame: then the served ball flies into the frame from the {side} edge.
Team sheet (shirt numbers seen in this match):
Watch frame by frame and answer:
seen           - true if you see the {team} team's serve (the server, or the served ball entering from the {side}) in this video
server_visible - true if the server is inside the frame when they hit the ball

t              - time in seconds from the start of this video (one decimal): the moment the server's hand strikes the ball (not the toss) if the server is visible; otherwise the first frame in which the served ball appears
number         - the server's shirt number, only if the server is visible and you can read it on their shirt, else null"""
SERVE_BEFORE, SERVE_AFTER = 1.5, 3.5    # check window around the scout's serve time
SERVE_GAP = 4.0                         # two serves this close are one serve seen twice
"""A serve is followed by at least a few seconds of play: serves closer than SERVE_GAP are duplicates
(overlapping clips, or toss and hit logged separately). Keep the one furthest from its clip's edge."""
prior = next((o for o in reversed(out) if o["type"] == "serve"), None) if e["type"] == "serve" else None
if prior is not None and e["t"] - prior["t"] < SERVE_GAP:
"""The clip scout logs serves about a second early (the toss, or a guess). A short high-fps look around each
serve times it at the hand-ball contact, or, when the server stands outside the frame, at the first frame
the served ball appears; it also reads the server's number when the server is in frame."""
prompt = SERVE_CHECK.format(length=t1 - t0, side="left" if team == "white" else "right",
a = match.watch_range(t0, t1, prompt, fps=10, model=tools.ARGON,
serves = [e for e in events if e["type"] == "serve"]
for e, r in zip(serves, match.map(one, serves)):
if not r or not isinstance(r[1], dict) or not r[1].get("seen"):
if t is not None and e["t"] - 0.5 <= t <= e["t"] + 2.5:
return [{"t": e["t"], "type": e["type"], "team": e["team"], "number": e.get("number")} for e in events]
conjecture: Serves are the one event class with a systematic timing error: the clip scout logs them 0.6-1.7 s before the scout's sheet (serve->receive gap is ~1.0 s in the sheet but 1.2-2.2 s in the system), turning about 6 set-1 serves into missed+invented pairs, and overlapping clips or toss/hit produce duplicate serves (1351, 1742, 1769). The server is often outside the side-on frame; the scout then times the serve at the moment the ball enters the frame (checked: the ball enters at ~1117.4, scout 1117.33).
prediction:
set 1: time F1 +0.02 to +0.03 (about 6 serve pairs fixed, 3-4 duplicate serves removed), OVERALL about 0.825; set 2 similar gain, about 0.83; cost +$1.3-1.6 per match (~45 serve checks at ~$0.03), so about $19.3/match; fitness about 0.79
Measured: set 1 0.819 (number 0.665), set 2 (unseen) 0.857 (number 0.702), $21.38/match
checks:
agent worked 6.1 min, 45 steps: I added a serve-timing stage to `system.py`, and `smoke.py` runs cleanly. I haven't scored it: the harness will run sets 1 and 2.

**The error I targeted:** the system's serve times are usually 0.6–1.7 s earlier than the scout's. On the scout's sheet, a serve comes about 1.0 s before the receive; in the system's output the gap is 1.2–2.2 s. That turns about 6 set-1 serves into a missed plus an invented event. There are also about 4 duplicate serves a second or so apart (around 1351, 1742 and 1769 s).

**The new stages:**
1. **One serve per rally:** if two serves are less than 4 s apart, only the one seen further from its clip's edge is kept. This is plain code and costs nothing.
2. **Serve check:** for each serve, Argon watches 5 s of video at 10 fps around it. It returns the moment the server hits the ball. If the server is outside the frame, it returns the moment the ball first appears. The time is changed only if the new one lies between 0.5 s before and 2.5 s after the old one. The shirt number is changed only when the server is visible. The check never deletes an event.

**What I found while testing:**
- **The server is often out of frame.** A free-text description of one window put the ball entering from the right edge at about 1117.4 s, and the scout's serve is at 1117.33. So the scout seems to log the serve when the ball comes into view. That is why the check asks for frame-entry time when it can't see the server.
- **Flash wasn't good enough.** It missed two of three
